hints.title: Connecting Horizontal Siblings in General Trees
hints.text: Unlike perfect binary trees, branches may have missing children. How can already established horizontal links on one tier help sew connections for the tier below?

hints.title: Dummy Head Needle for Next Tier
hints.text: Use a dummy sentinel node to anchor the beginning of the next level. As you traverse across the current level using established next links, append each child to the tail of the next level.

hints.title: Constant Space Two-Tier Iteration Blueprint
hints.text: Outer loop starts at root. For each tier, initialize dummy and tail. While current node is not null, if left child exists attach to tail and advance tail; do the same for right child. Advance current via current.next. Move down to dummy.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in binary tree
complexity.notes: Visits every node and edge exactly once with constant auxiliary pointers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard level-order collections require O(W) auxiliary memory where W is maximum tree width.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Leveraging established horizontal links as linked lists achieves O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly handling non-full trees with scattered leaves and missing left or right children.
